clusters.name: cluster-preflight
clusters.executionModeRationale: Standalone validation gate with no committed code overlap; must complete and pass before the build commits.

clusters.name: cluster-server
clusters.executionModeRationale: All three stories edit the same happy-server auth surface (the security core) and must run serially within one cluster; this is the highest-risk work and the contract every other cluster binds to.

clusters.name: cluster-cli
clusters.executionModeRationale: happy-cli is a separate package with no file overlap with happy-app or codex, so it runs in parallel with cluster-app once the server contract is frozen; depends on cluster-server so the LAN bind is never permitted without the verifier.

clusters.name: cluster-app
clusters.executionModeRationale: Both stories edit the same happy-app sync/auth/settings + i18n surface and must run serially within the cluster; the cluster is a separate package from cli/codex so it runs in parallel with cluster-cli.

clusters.name: cluster-codex
clusters.executionModeRationale: codex is a separate submodule repo (own worktree + two-commit flow); depends on cluster-cli so the transport it gates exists, but is otherwise file-disjoint.

clusters.name: cluster-docs
clusters.executionModeRationale: Documentation records the final reviewed model, so it lands last after every code cluster; low risk but depends on all to describe the shipped behavior accurately.
